cards.text: Paul, the apostle, is writing to the believers in Rome. He's just told them to pay everyone what they owe: taxes, respect, honor (Romans 13:7). Now he names the one debt they're supposed to keep on owing.

cards.question: Paul tells the believers in Rome to be indebted to no one, except to one another in ___.
Paul says the one who loves his neighbor has ___ the law.

cards.text: Then Paul lists commandments: “Do not commit adultery,” “Do not murder,” “Do not steal,” “Do not covet.” And any other commandments too, friend, ALL of them, and he says they get packed into one cookie box.

cards.question: Paul says all those commandments, and every other one, are summed up in one decree. Which one?
True or false: Paul says love does no wrong to its neighbor.

cards.text: So love does no wrong to its neighbor, and that makes love the fulfillment of the law. The WHOLE law in one word, and I can't put two toppings on one cookie without causing an avalanche.
Then Paul says, “And do this, understanding the occasion.” Translation: friend, take a look at the clock.

cards.question: Paul tells the believers in Rome the hour has come for them to do what?
Paul says it's time to wake up, because their ___ is nearer now than when they first believed.

cards.text: No snooze button. No "five more minutes." Trust me, after years in a junk drawer I KNOW what a long nap does to you, and Paul says the night is nearly over and the day has drawn near.

cards.question: With the night nearly over, Paul says to lay aside the deeds of darkness and put on what?

cards.text: Paul says to behave decently, as in the daytime. Then he names what that leaves behind, and friend, some of it might surprise you.

cards.question: True or false: Paul puts dissension and jealousy on the same list as drunkenness.

cards.text: Instead of all that, Paul tells them what to put on. And no, friend, it's not an apron. I checked. TWICE.

cards.question: Instead of the deeds of darkness, Paul says to clothe yourselves with whom?
True or false: Paul says to leave a little room for the desires of the flesh, just in case.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 4 quotes "Do not covet.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The joke puts the cookie box inside Paul's teaching: "he says they get packed into one cookie box." The comparison is blended into the Bible setting and reads as something Paul said. Romans 13:9 says the commandments are "summed up in this one decree."

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The card opens by repeating what card 6 just asked: "So love does no wrong to its neighbor." It restates the answer the baker just gave instead of moving the passage forward.
"The WHOLE law in one word" renames what the text calls "this one decree" (Romans 13:9). The line also draws on verse 9, but the card cites only Romans 13:10.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The drawer joke treats his drawer years as "a long nap," but being stuck in the drawer isn't sleeping. The backstory has him lying awake in the dark. The action doesn't match Paul's call to wake from slumber.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: "The robes of morning" is not a real detail from the Bible. It is also close in meaning to the right answer, since both are day or light clothing to put on, so a baker could argue it's right.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: "Some of it might surprise you" tips the true or false on card 14 toward True and rules out False before the baker reasons it out.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The full list in Romans 13:13 is never told. Carousing, sexual immorality and debauchery never appear on any card. Card 14 only mentions dissension, jealousy and drunkenness.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
